questions.promptHtml:
A freight company receives many supplier invoices each day as files in Amazon S3. Each invoice goes through the same four steps in the same order. A model in Amazon Bedrock extracts the invoice fields. Code compares the fields with the matching order record. A model writes a short note about any difference. Code sends the result to the finance system.
Every invoice must pass all four steps, with no step skipped. Auditors must see the input and the output of each step for any invoice of the last 30 days.
Which design will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
questions.promptText:
A freight company receives many supplier invoices each day as files in Amazon S3. Each invoice goes through the same four steps in the same order. A model in Amazon Bedrock extracts the invoice fields. Code compares the fields with the matching order record. A model writes a short note about any difference. Code sends the result to the finance system.
Every invoice must pass all four steps, with no step skipped. Auditors must see the input and the output of each step for any invoice of the last 30 days.
Which design will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create one AWS Lambda function that asks the model, in one prompt, to extract the fields, compare them with the matching order record and write the note, and then sends the answer to the finance system.
Run a script on an Amazon EC2 instance that runs the four steps in order for each invoice and writes the input and the output of each step to a log file.
Create an AWS Step Functions Standard workflow with one state for each step, and call the model through the optimized integration for Amazon Bedrock in the two model states.
Create an agent in Amazon Bedrock Agents with an action group for each step, and write agent instructions that tell the agent to run the four steps in order.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Create an AWS Step Functions Standard workflow with one state for each step, and call the model through the optimized integration for Amazon Bedrock in the two model states.
A Step Functions state machine runs the states that the team defines, in the order that the definition sets. The steps of this task are known in advance and never change, so a fixed workflow fits them. The optimized integration lets a state call InvokeModel in Amazon Bedrock directly.

A Standard workflow keeps the history of each execution for 90 days, and the Step Functions console shows the input and the output of every state, which gives the auditors what they need. Step Functions is a managed service, so the team runs no servers.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.1.1: "Create comprehensive architectural designs that align with specific business needs and technical constraints"
Example: "integration patterns"

Sources:

  • Invoke and customize Amazon Bedrock models with Step Functions
  • Viewing execution details in the Step Functions console
  • How Amazon Bedrock Agents works

INCORRECT: Create one AWS Lambda function that asks the model, in one prompt, to extract the fields, compare them with the matching order record and write the note, and then sends the answer to the finance system.
This design puts three steps into one model call. The comparison with the matching order record then comes from the model, not from code, and nothing makes sure that the model performs every step. The auditors also see one input and one answer for each invoice, not the input and the output of each step.

INCORRECT: Run a script on an Amazon EC2 instance that runs the four steps in order for each invoice and writes the input and the output of each step to a log file.
A script can run the steps in a fixed order and write a log for the auditors. However, the team must run and patch the instance, scale it for the daily volume, write its own error handling and keep the log files. That is more operational overhead than a managed workflow service that records each step for every execution.

INCORRECT: Create an agent in Amazon Bedrock Agents with an action group for each step, and write agent instructions that tell the agent to run the four steps in order.
An agent uses a foundation model to decide what to do next. At each step of the orchestration, the model predicts which action to call or which knowledge base to query. The instructions can ask for a fixed order, but the model still makes the choice, so the team cannot be sure that every invoice passes all four steps.

An agent fits a task where the model must choose the steps or the tools. In this task, the steps are always the same.

questions.promptHtml:
A recruiting company plans a feature that turns the notes of a hiring manager into a short job post. A model in Amazon Bedrock will write each post. The team has three candidate models and 10 sample notes, and it works in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio.
Before anyone writes code, the product manager wants to read the posts of all three models for the same note at the same time. The product manager also wants to change the system instructions and the temperature, and then see new posts at once.
Which feature should the team use?
questions.promptText:
A recruiting company plans a feature that turns the notes of a hiring manager into a short job post. A model in Amazon Bedrock will write each post. The team has three candidate models and 10 sample notes, and it works in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio.
Before anyone writes code, the product manager wants to read the posts of all three models for the same note at the same time. The product manager also wants to change the system instructions and the temperature, and then see new posts at once.
Which feature should the team use?

options.text: Create an automatic model evaluation job in Amazon Bedrock for each candidate model, with the sample notes as a custom prompt dataset in Amazon S3.
Turn on compare mode in the Amazon Bedrock chat playground, select one candidate model in each chat window, and enter each sample note.
Write an AWS Lambda function that sends each sample note to the three models, and store the posts in Amazon S3 for the product manager to read.
Create an Amazon Bedrock intelligent prompt router with the three candidate models, and send each sample note to the router.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Turn on compare mode in the Amazon Bedrock chat playground, select one candidate model in each chat window, and enter each sample note.
The chat playground in SageMaker Unified Studio has a compare mode. With compare mode on, the team selects a model in each chat window, enters a prompt and sees the output of each model. The playground can compare up to three models, which matches the three candidates.

The product manager can also change model settings, such as the inference parameters and the system instructions, run the note again and compare the new results. No code is needed, which fits a proof of concept at this early stage.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.1.2: "Develop technical proof-of-concept implementations to validate feasibility, performance characteristics, and business value before proceeding to full-scale deployment"
Example: "Amazon Bedrock"

Sources:

  • Chat with a model in the Amazon Bedrock chat playground
  • Use prompt datasets for model evaluation in Amazon Bedrock
  • Understanding intelligent prompt routing in Amazon Bedrock

INCORRECT: Create an automatic model evaluation job in Amazon Bedrock for each candidate model, with the sample notes as a custom prompt dataset in Amazon S3.
An automatic model evaluation job sends every prompt of a JSON Lines dataset in Amazon S3 to the model and scores the answers. It is a good tool later, when the team has a dataset and clear metrics.

Here, the product manager wants to read the posts side by side and change the instructions and the temperature while reading. A job uses the settings that the team gives it when the job starts, so each change means another job.

INCORRECT: Write an AWS Lambda function that sends each sample note to the three models, and store the posts in Amazon S3 for the product manager to read.
A Lambda function can call the three models and save the posts. However, the product manager wants to read posts before anyone writes code. Each change of the instructions or the temperature would also need another run of the function, so new posts would not appear at once.

INCORRECT: Create an Amazon Bedrock intelligent prompt router with the three candidate models, and send each sample note to the router.
Intelligent prompt routing gives a single endpoint that routes each request to one of the models of the same model family. The product manager would see one post for each note, not the posts of all three models. In the console, a router also takes exactly two models.

questions.promptHtml:
A university gives each research lab its own AWS account. All lab accounts are in one organizational unit (OU) in AWS Organizations, and new labs join every term. The platform team wrote one AWS CloudFormation template with the approved setup for generative AI work: an Amazon Bedrock guardrail, an IAM role for applications that call Amazon Bedrock, and Amazon CloudWatch alarms on Amazon Bedrock metrics.
Every lab account must have this setup in two AWS Regions, including accounts that join later. A new account must receive the setup with no manual step.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
questions.promptText:
A university gives each research lab its own AWS account. All lab accounts are in one organizational unit (OU) in AWS Organizations, and new labs join every term. The platform team wrote one AWS CloudFormation template with the approved setup for generative AI work: an Amazon Bedrock guardrail, an IAM role for applications that call Amazon Bedrock, and Amazon CloudWatch alarms on Amazon Bedrock metrics.
Every lab account must have this setup in two AWS Regions, including accounts that join later. A new account must receive the setup with no manual step.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Share the template with the lab teams, and ask each lab to create a stack from the template in both Regions when its account joins the OU.
Create a CloudFormation StackSet with self-managed permissions from the template, and deploy stack instances to the account IDs of the current lab accounts in both Regions.
Create the guardrail in the management account in both Regions, and attach an Amazon Bedrock policy to the lab OU that enforces the guardrail in every lab account.
Create a CloudFormation StackSet with service-managed permissions from the template, target the lab OU in both Regions, and turn on automatic deployment.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Create a CloudFormation StackSet with service-managed permissions from the template, target the lab OU in both Regions, and turn on automatic deployment.
A StackSet deploys one template to many accounts and Regions. With service-managed permissions, StackSets works with AWS Organizations and creates the IAM roles that it needs on its own. This permission model also supports automatic deployment. When an account is added to the target OU, StackSets creates a stack instance in that account in each target Region. New lab accounts receive the guardrail, the role and the alarms with no manual step.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.1.3: "Create standardized technical components to ensure consistent implementation across multiple deployment scenarios"

Sources:

  • StackSets concepts
  • Enable or disable automatic deployments for StackSets in AWS Organizations
  • Amazon Bedrock policies

INCORRECT: Share the template with the lab teams, and ask each lab to create a stack from the template in both Regions when its account joins the OU.
Each lab could create a stack from the shared template. This needs a person in each lab to act when the account joins, and a lab can forget a Region or change the template. The requirements ask for no manual step, so this solution does not meet them.

INCORRECT: Create a CloudFormation StackSet with self-managed permissions from the template, and deploy stack instances to the account IDs of the current lab accounts in both Regions.
With self-managed permissions, the team creates the IAM roles that StackSets needs in each target account. Automatic deployment to accounts that join the organization later comes with service-managed permissions. With this solution, each new lab account would need the roles and a new deployment by hand, and the requirements allow no manual step.

INCORRECT: Create the guardrail in the management account in both Regions, and attach an Amazon Bedrock policy to the lab OU that enforces the guardrail in every lab account.
An Amazon Bedrock policy in AWS Organizations references a guardrail in the management account and enforces it on the model calls of every account under the OU, new accounts included. This covers the guardrail part of the setup. However, the policy enforces a guardrail only. It does not create the IAM role or the CloudWatch alarms in each lab account, so the approved setup is not complete.

questions.promptHtml:
A home insurance company is building an app for damage claims. A customer uploads a photo of the damage and writes a few sentences about it. A model in Amazon Bedrock reads both and writes a first estimate. The app streams the estimate to the customer while the model writes it.
The team took eight candidate models from a public ranking of text tasks. The team wants to remove the models that cannot do this job before it spends time on tests.
Which step should the team take FIRST?
questions.promptText:
A home insurance company is building an app for damage claims. A customer uploads a photo of the damage and writes a few sentences about it. A model in Amazon Bedrock reads both and writes a first estimate. The app streams the estimate to the customer while the model writes it.
The team took eight candidate models from a public ranking of text tasks. The team wants to remove the models that cannot do this job before it spends time on tests.
Which step should the team take FIRST?

options.text: Read the model card of each candidate in the Amazon Bedrock documentation, and keep only the models that list image input and response streaming.
Create an automatic model evaluation job in Amazon Bedrock for each candidate, with a prompt dataset of past claim texts in Amazon S3.
Keep the three models with the highest scores in the public ranking, and test them in the app with sample claims.
Create an Amazon Bedrock intelligent prompt router with the candidate models, so that the router sends each claim to a model that can read it.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Read the model card of each candidate in the Amazon Bedrock documentation, and keep only the models that list image input and response streaming.
The model card of a model in the Amazon Bedrock documentation lists its input and output modalities and the features that it supports, such as response streaming. Support differs from model to model. For example, the model card of Amazon Nova Micro lists text as its only input modality, so that model cannot read the photo. A quick check of the cards removes such models before the team spends time on any test.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.2.1: "Assess and choose FMs to ensure optimal alignment with specific business use cases and technical requirements"
Example: "capability analysis"

Sources:

  • Nova Micro
  • Use prompt datasets for model evaluation in Amazon Bedrock
  • Understanding intelligent prompt routing in Amazon Bedrock

INCORRECT: Create an automatic model evaluation job in Amazon Bedrock for each candidate, with a prompt dataset of past claim texts in Amazon S3.
An automatic model evaluation job sends each prompt of a dataset to the model and scores the answers. A dataset of claim texts tests text only, so it shows nothing about the photo or the streaming. A job is also a test, and the team wants to remove the unfit models before it spends time on tests.

INCORRECT: Keep the three models with the highest scores in the public ranking, and test them in the app with sample claims.
The public ranking measures text tasks. It says nothing about whether a model accepts an image or streams its output. A model at the top of the ranking can still accept text only, and the team would then spend time testing a model that cannot read the photo.

INCORRECT: Create an Amazon Bedrock intelligent prompt router with the candidate models, so that the router sends each claim to a model that can read it.
Intelligent prompt routing gives a single endpoint that routes requests between models of the same model family. It picks one model for each request. It does not check which models accept an image, and it does not narrow a list of candidates before tests.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
questions.promptHtml:
A travel company's trip planner writes a day-by-day plan for each customer. Three AWS Lambda functions call a model in Amazon Bedrock with the InvokeModel API. Each function builds a request body in the format of the current provider's model, and the model ID is written in the function code.
In the coming months, the company will test chat models from other providers. The team must be able to switch all three functions to a chat model from any provider in Amazon Bedrock with no change to the function code.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements?
Select TWO.
questions.promptText:
A travel company's trip planner writes a day-by-day plan for each customer. Three AWS Lambda functions call a model in Amazon Bedrock with the InvokeModel API. Each function builds a request body in the format of the current provider's model, and the model ID is written in the function code.
In the coming months, the company will test chat models from other providers. The team must be able to switch all three functions to a chat model from any provider in Amazon Bedrock with no change to the function code.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements?
Select TWO.

options.text: Keep the InvokeModel API, and add a request body builder to each function for every provider that the team plans to test.
Change each function to call the Converse API, which uses one request format for all Amazon Bedrock models that support messages.
Create an Amazon Bedrock intelligent prompt router with the current model and a model from another provider, and call the router from each function.
Publish a new version of each function for each candidate model, and point a Lambda alias at the version with the chosen model ID.
Store the model ID in AWS AppConfig, and have each function read the deployed value at runtime through the AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Change each function to call the Converse API, which uses one request format for all Amazon Bedrock models that support messages.
The Converse API gives one consistent request format that works with all Amazon Bedrock models that support messages. The team writes the call once and uses it with different models. After this change, a switch to another provider's chat model needs only a new model ID, not a new request body.

CORRECT: Store the model ID in AWS AppConfig, and have each function read the deployed value at runtime through the AWS AppConfig Agent Lambda extension.
AWS AppConfig changes application behavior in production without a new code deployment. Each function reads the configuration from a local endpoint of AWS AppConfig Agent, which caches the deployed value. When the team deploys a new model ID in AWS AppConfig, all three functions use the new model, and the function code stays the same.

Together with the Converse API, this step turns a provider switch into a configuration change.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.2.2: "Create flexible architecture patterns to enable dynamic model selection and provider switching without requiring code modifications"
Example: "AWS AppConfig"

Sources:

  • Inference using Converse API
  • What is AWS AppConfig?
  • Understanding intelligent prompt routing in Amazon Bedrock

INCORRECT: Keep the InvokeModel API, and add a request body builder to each function for every provider that the team plans to test.
Builders for the planned providers would let the functions call those models. However, the team must be able to switch to a chat model from any provider in Amazon Bedrock. A provider that is not on the current list would need another builder, which is a code change. The model ID is also still written in the code.

INCORRECT: Create an Amazon Bedrock intelligent prompt router with the current model and a model from another provider, and call the router from each function.
Intelligent prompt routing routes requests between models of the same model family. A router cannot combine the models of two providers, and it chooses the model for each request on its own. The team wants to choose the model itself.

INCORRECT: Publish a new version of each function for each candidate model, and point a Lambda alias at the version with the chosen model ID.
In this plan, each version has the model ID written in its code, so every new candidate model means new code and a new version. The request body also stays in the format of the current provider, so a model from another provider would not accept it.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
questions.promptHtml:
An engineering firm runs an internal search site for its project documents. For each search, an AWS Lambda function queries an Amazon OpenSearch Service index. The function then calls a model in Amazon Bedrock to write a short summary above the results. Last week, the model calls returned ServiceUnavailable errors for about 20 minutes, and every search showed an error page.
A model error that lasts only a short time must not stop the summary. When the model still fails, employees must still see the search results. Only this model is approved, and all requests must stay in the current AWS Region.
Which actions should the team take?
Select TWO.
questions.promptText:
An engineering firm runs an internal search site for its project documents. For each search, an AWS Lambda function queries an Amazon OpenSearch Service index. The function then calls a model in Amazon Bedrock to write a short summary above the results. Last week, the model calls returned ServiceUnavailable errors for about 20 minutes, and every search showed an error page.
A model error that lasts only a short time must not stop the summary. When the model still fails, employees must still see the search results. Only this model is approved, and all requests must stay in the current AWS Region.
Which actions should the team take?
Select TWO.

options.text: Configure the AWS SDK client in the function to retry failed model calls in standard retry mode, with exponential backoff and jitter.
Call the model through a cross-Region inference profile, so that Amazon Bedrock can send requests to other AWS Regions when the current Region is busy.
Catch the error that remains after the last retry, and send the request to a model from another provider to write the summary.
Catch the error that remains after the last retry, and return the search results with a short note that no summary is available.
Raise the timeout of the Lambda function to the maximum, so that the function waits until the model can answer again.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Configure the AWS SDK client in the function to retry failed model calls in standard retry mode, with exponential backoff and jitter.
ServiceUnavailable is a temporary error, and the Amazon Bedrock documentation suggests retries with exponential backoff and random jitter for it. In standard retry mode, the AWS SDK retries a failed request with exponential backoff and jitter. An error that lasts only a short time then usually ends with a successful retry, and the summary still appears. When the last attempt fails, the SDK returns the error to the function code.

CORRECT: Catch the error that remains after the last retry, and return the search results with a short note that no summary is available.
This step is graceful degradation. The search results come from OpenSearch Service and do not depend on the model. When the model still fails after the retries, the function catches the final error and returns the results without a summary. Employees can still search while the model is not available, and they see results instead of an error page.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.2.3: "Design resilient AI systems to ensure continuous operation during service disruptions"
Example: "graceful degradation strategies"

Sources:

  • Troubleshooting Amazon Bedrock API Error Codes
  • Retry behavior
  • REL05-BP01 Implement graceful degradation to transform applicable hard dependencies into soft dependencies

INCORRECT: Call the model through a cross-Region inference profile, so that Amazon Bedrock can send requests to other AWS Regions when the current Region is busy.
Cross-Region inference routes requests by using compute in other AWS Regions, and the Amazon Bedrock documentation suggests it when ServiceUnavailable errors continue in one Region. However, all requests must stay in the current Region, so this action breaks a stated requirement.

INCORRECT: Catch the error that remains after the last retry, and send the request to a model from another provider to write the summary.
A fallback to another model is a common resilience pattern. In this company, only the current model is approved, so the function cannot send the documents to a model from another provider.

INCORRECT: Raise the timeout of the Lambda function to the maximum, so that the function waits until the model can answer again.
A longer timeout gives a slow call more time to finish. A ServiceUnavailable error is a response from the service, so more time does not make a new attempt. With no retry and no fallback, employees would still see an error page when the model call fails.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
questions.promptHtml:
A retailer prepares customer reviews each night in an AWS Glue ETL job, and a model in Amazon Bedrock then writes a review summary for each product. Twice this quarter, the summaries were poor. First, a partner sent many reviews with a null value in the review text column. Later, a change in another system cut the number of distinct products in half. Both times, the data quality rules in the job passed.
Review volume changes by weekday and by season. The team cannot know which column or statistic will change next.
Which solution will catch changes like these in later runs?
questions.promptText:
A retailer prepares customer reviews each night in an AWS Glue ETL job, and a model in Amazon Bedrock then writes a review summary for each product. Twice this quarter, the summaries were poor. First, a partner sent many reviews with a null value in the review text column. Later, a change in another system cut the number of distinct products in half. Both times, the data quality rules in the job passed.
Review volume changes by weekday and by season. The team cannot know which column or statistic will change next.
Which solution will catch changes like these in later runs?

options.text: Create a Data Quality and Insights report in Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler on the review data, and read the report when the summaries look poor.
Add dynamic rules to the ruleset that compare the completeness of the review text and the distinct count of product IDs with the average of the last 10 runs.
Add analyzers for the review columns to the AWS Glue Data Quality ruleset, and turn on anomaly detection, which learns from the statistics of past runs.
Add fixed rules to the ruleset for each column, such as a minimum row count and a minimum completeness of the review text.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Add analyzers for the review columns to the AWS Glue Data Quality ruleset, and turn on anomaly detection, which learns from the statistics of past runs.
Analyzers gather statistics about the data, such as completeness and distinct values, without explicit rules. Anomaly detection in AWS Glue Data Quality learns from these statistics over time and predicts a range for each value. When an actual value falls outside its range, AWS Glue Data Quality creates an anomaly observation.

The algorithm can also learn seasonal patterns, such as weekdays that differ from weekends. The team does not need to know in advance which statistic will change. Anomaly detection needs at least three data points before it can detect anomalies.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.3.1: "Create comprehensive data validation workflows to ensure data meets quality standards for FM consumption"
Example: "AWS Glue Data Quality"

Sources:

  • Anomaly detection in AWS Glue Data Quality
  • Data Quality Definition Language (DQDL) reference
  • Get Insights On Data and Data Quality

INCORRECT: Create a Data Quality and Insights report in Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler on the review data, and read the report when the summaries look poor.
This report shows information such as missing values and outliers for data that the team imported into Data Wrangler. The team creates the report on request from a node in a flow. It does not check each nightly run, and the team would read it only after the summaries are already poor.

INCORRECT: Add dynamic rules to the ruleset that compare the completeness of the review text and the distinct count of product IDs with the average of the last 10 runs.
Dynamic rules compare a metric of the current run with its values in past runs, for example with the average of the last runs. These two rules would catch the two past problems. However, each dynamic rule checks one statistic that the team picks. The team cannot know which column or statistic will change next, so a change in another column would still pass.

INCORRECT: Add fixed rules to the ruleset for each column, such as a minimum row count and a minimum completeness of the review text.
Fixed rules check the data against fixed criteria. Review volume changes by weekday and by season, so one minimum row count is too high on some days and too low on others. Fixed rules also check only what the team writes into them, and the existing rules in the job passed both times.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
questions.promptHtml:
An online marketplace wants a model in Amazon Bedrock to write a short title for each of its product listings. Each listing is a row in a database table with a listing ID. The company needs the titles by the next morning, so the team chose batch inference with the default model invocation type.
Each title must be saved to the row of the listing that it belongs to.
How should the team prepare the input data?
questions.promptText:
An online marketplace wants a model in Amazon Bedrock to write a short title for each of its product listings. Each listing is a row in a database table with a listing ID. The company needs the titles by the next morning, so the team chose batch inference with the default model invocation type.
Each title must be saved to the row of the listing that it belongs to.
How should the team prepare the input data?

options.text: Write a JSONL file in which each line has a modelInput that matches the InvokeModel request body of the chosen model, in the order of the table rows, and match each output line to a listing by its line number.
Write a JSONL file in which each line has the listing ID as the recordId and a modelInput that matches the InvokeModel request body of the chosen model.
Write a CSV file with one row for each listing, with a column for the listing ID and a column for the listing text.
Write a JSONL file in which each line has the listing ID as the recordId and a modelInput that contains only the listing text as a plain string.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Write a JSONL file in which each line has the listing ID as the recordId and a modelInput that matches the InvokeModel request body of the chosen model.
Batch inference reads a JSONL file in which each line has a recordId and a modelInput. With the default InvokeModel type, the modelInput must match the body that the chosen model takes in an InvokeModel request. The order of the records in the output file can differ from the order in the input file. Each output record carries the recordId of its input, so the listing ID links every title to the right row.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.3.3: "Format input data for FM inference according to model-specific requirements"
Example: "JSON formatting for Amazon Bedrock API requests"

Sources:

  • Format and upload your batch inference data
  • View the results of a batch inference job

INCORRECT: Write a JSONL file in which each line has a modelInput that matches the InvokeModel request body of the chosen model, in the order of the table rows, and match each output line to a listing by its line number.
The format of each modelInput is right, but the plan depends on the line order. Amazon Bedrock does not guarantee that the output records come in the same order as the input records, so titles could reach the wrong listings. When the input has no recordId, Amazon Bedrock adds its own IDs in the output, and these IDs do not match the listing IDs.

INCORRECT: Write a CSV file with one row for each listing, with a column for the listing ID and a column for the listing text.
Batch inference input is a JSONL file, which must end in the .jsonl extension, with one JSON object on each line. A CSV file does not have this format, and it has no modelInput in the request format of the model.

INCORRECT: Write a JSONL file in which each line has the listing ID as the recordId and a modelInput that contains only the listing text as a plain string.
The recordId part of this plan is right. However, with the default InvokeModel type, the modelInput must match the InvokeModel request body of the chosen model. A plain string does not match that body, so the model input is not valid.

Long emails often name several products and dates. Claims staff find that many forms show a product name or a date that is not in the email. Each form must use only names and dates from the email, and the summary must cover the whole email. The team wants no model training.
How should the team prepare the input for the model?

Long emails often name several products and dates. Claims staff find that many forms show a product name or a date that is not in the email. Each form must use only names and dates from the email, and the summary must cover the whole email. The team wants no model training.

options.text: Call Amazon Comprehend DetectEntities on each email, and add the COMMERCIAL_ITEM and DATE entities that it finds to the prompt as labeled fields, together with the full email.
Call Amazon Comprehend DetectKeyPhrases on each email, and add the key phrases that it finds to the prompt as labeled product and date fields, together with the full email.
Call Amazon Comprehend DetectEntities on each email, and send only the COMMERCIAL_ITEM and DATE entities that it finds to the model, in place of the email.
Train an Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognizer on past claim emails, and add the products and dates that it finds to the prompt as labeled fields, together with the full email.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Call Amazon Comprehend DetectEntities on each email, and add the COMMERCIAL_ITEM and DATE entities that it finds to the prompt as labeled fields, together with the full email.
DetectEntities is the Amazon Comprehend operation that finds predefined entity types in text. Each result gives the text of the entity, its type and a confidence score. The type COMMERCIAL_ITEM marks a branded product, and the type DATE marks a full date, a day, a month or a time.

The Lambda function places these values in the prompt under clear labels, such as Products and Dates, next to the full email. The model then works with values that Amazon Comprehend took from the email text, and it still reads the whole email for the summary. No model is trained, because these entity types are built in.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.3.4: "Enhance input data quality to improve FM response quality and consistency"
Example: "Amazon Comprehend to extract entities"

Sources:

  • Entities
  • Key phrases
  • Custom entity recognition

INCORRECT: Call Amazon Comprehend DetectKeyPhrases on each email, and add the key phrases that it finds to the prompt as labeled product and date fields, together with the full email.
DetectKeyPhrases returns noun phrases, such as "the zipper on my jacket", with a confidence score for each one. A key phrase has no type. The function cannot tell which phrases are products and which are dates, so it cannot fill labeled product and date fields from this result.

INCORRECT: Call Amazon Comprehend DetectEntities on each email, and send only the COMMERCIAL_ITEM and DATE entities that it finds to the model, in place of the email.
This option uses the right Amazon Comprehend operation, but it removes the email from the request. The model receives a list of products and dates with no text around them. It cannot write a summary of the problem, because only the email describes the problem, and the summary must cover the whole email.

INCORRECT: Train an Amazon Comprehend custom entity recognizer on past claim emails, and add the products and dates that it finds to the prompt as labeled fields, together with the full email.
A custom entity recognizer is an Amazon Comprehend model that a company trains with its own annotations or entity lists. It finds entity types that the built-in model does not know, such as internal product codes. Here, products and dates are already built-in entity types, and the team wants no model training.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
questions.promptHtml:
A retail company runs a human resources (HR) assistant for its store staff. The assistant calls the Retrieve API of an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. The knowledge base has an Amazon S3 data source that contains the HR policies.
The HR team uploads each new or changed policy to the data source as soon as it is approved, up to 60 days before the policy takes effect. On the day a new version takes effect, a daily job deletes the old version. Staff now receive answers from policies that are not in force yet.
Which combination of steps will solve this issue with the LEAST operational overhead?
Select TWO.
questions.promptText:
A retail company runs a human resources (HR) assistant for its store staff. The assistant calls the Retrieve API of an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. The knowledge base has an Amazon S3 data source that contains the HR policies.
The HR team uploads each new or changed policy to the data source as soon as it is approved, up to 60 days before the policy takes effect. On the day a new version takes effect, a daily job deletes the old version. Staff now receive answers from policies that are not in force yet.
Which combination of steps will solve this issue with the LEAST operational overhead?
Select TWO.

options.text: Add the effective date to the first page of each policy, and add an instruction to the prompt that tells the model to ignore any policy that is not in force yet.
Add a metadata file next to each policy in the S3 bucket with an effective_date attribute of type NUMBER, such as 20261101, and sync the data source.
Add an Amazon Bedrock reranker model to each Retrieve request, so the policies with the newest dates move to the top of the results.
Add a filter to each Retrieve request that uses the lessThanOrEquals operator on the effective_date attribute, with the current date as a number.

Create an Amazon EventBridge Scheduler schedule that runs an AWS Lambda function each night. The function moves the policies that take effect the next day from a staging prefix into the data source and starts a sync.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Add a metadata file next to each policy in the S3 bucket with an effective_date attribute of type NUMBER, such as 20261101, and sync the data source.
A knowledge base with an S3 data source reads the attributes of each document from a metadata file in the same folder. The file has the name of the document with .metadata.json added at the end. The type NUMBER matters here, because the range operators of a metadata filter accept only numbers. A date written as a number, such as 20261101, keeps the order of the dates: a bigger number is a later date. After the sync, each policy in the knowledge base has its effective date.

CORRECT: Add a filter to each Retrieve request that uses the lessThanOrEquals operator on the effective_date attribute, with the current date as a number.
A filter in the Retrieve request limits the search to the chunks whose metadata matches the filter. With lessThanOrEquals and the current date, such as 20261020, the search returns only policies whose effective date has arrived. A policy that takes effect next month stays in the bucket and in the knowledge base, but no search returns it before its date. The HR team keeps its upload process, and the company runs no extra job.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.4.2: "Develop comprehensive metadata frameworks to improve search precision and context awareness for FM interactions"

Sources:

  • Connect to Amazon S3 for your knowledge base
  • Configure and customize queries and response generation

INCORRECT: Add the effective date to the first page of each policy, and add an instruction to the prompt that tells the model to ignore any policy that is not in force yet.
This step leaves the decision to the model. The search still returns rules from policies that are not in force, and the model can still use them, because only an instruction tells it not to. Also, the date on the first page is only in the first chunk of a policy. The other chunks of the same policy have no date, so the model cannot tell which of these rules are in force.

INCORRECT: Add an Amazon Bedrock reranker model to each Retrieve request, so the policies with the newest dates move to the top of the results.
A reranker model puts the results in a new order by how relevant each chunk is to the question. It is not a date rule, so a policy that is not in force yet can still be among the top results. Also, the policies with the newest dates are often the ones that are not in force yet, so this order would make the issue worse.

INCORRECT: Create an Amazon EventBridge Scheduler schedule that runs an AWS Lambda function each night. The function moves the policies that take effect the next day from a staging prefix into the data source and starts a sync.
This design can keep future policies out of the knowledge base until their date, so it would work. However, the company must write and run a Lambda function and a schedule, and the HR team must upload to a new staging prefix. A metadata filter is a built-in feature of the knowledge base, so it needs much less operational overhead.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
questions.promptHtml:
An engineering company runs a research assistant on Amazon OpenSearch Service. The domain runs a recent OpenSearch version. One k-NN index uses the FAISS engine and contains about 400 million chunk vectors from 2 million project reports. Most questions are about one to three reports.
Search latency grows each month as the company adds reports. The company must reduce the number of vectors that each query searches. It must keep the current number of nodes.
Which combination of steps should the company take?
Select TWO.
questions.promptText:
An engineering company runs a research assistant on Amazon OpenSearch Service. The domain runs a recent OpenSearch version. One k-NN index uses the FAISS engine and contains about 400 million chunk vectors from 2 million project reports. Most questions are about one to three reports.
Search latency grows each month as the company adds reports. The company must reduce the number of vectors that each query searches. It must keep the current number of nodes.
Which combination of steps should the company take?
Select TWO.

options.text: Create a second index with one summary vector for each report and its report ID. Search this index first to find the closest reports.
Add one summary vector for each report to the chunk index. Search the summaries and the chunks together in one k-NN query.
Run the k-NN query on the chunk index, and then remove the chunks of other reports with a post_filter on the report IDs.
Run the k-NN query on the chunk index with a filter inside the query that keeps only the chunks of the reports from the first search.
Split the chunk index into more shards on the current nodes, so that each shard contains fewer vectors.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Create a second index with one summary vector for each report and its report ID. Search this index first to find the closest reports.
A summary index contains 2 million vectors, one for each report, far fewer than the 400 million chunk vectors. Most questions are about one to three reports, so a search of the summaries can find these reports first. The report ID in each summary links the result to the chunks of the same report. This first search is small and fast.

CORRECT: Run the k-NN query on the chunk index with a filter inside the query that keeps only the chunks of the reports from the first search.
Amazon OpenSearch Service supports efficient filters in k-NN queries on the FAISS engine. With the filter inside the query, the search looks only at the chunks that match the filter, here the chunks of the few reports from the first search. Together with the summary index, each question searches a small part of the 400 million vectors, and the number of nodes stays the same.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.4.3: "Implement high-performance vector database architectures to optimize semantic search performance at scale for FM retrieval"
Example: "hierarchical indexing techniques"

Sources:

  • k-Nearest Neighbor (k-NN) search in Amazon OpenSearch Service
  • Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports efficient vector query filters for FAISS

INCORRECT: Add one summary vector for each report to the chunk index. Search the summaries and the chunks together in one k-NN query.
The summaries add 2 million more vectors to the chunk index. One query on this index still searches all the chunk vectors, plus the summaries. The number of vectors that each query searches grows, so this step works against the requirement.

INCORRECT: Run the k-NN query on the chunk index, and then remove the chunks of other reports with a post_filter on the report IDs.
A post_filter runs after the k-NN search. The search first runs over all chunk vectors, so the number of vectors that each query searches does not go down. The AWS documentation also warns that a k-NN query mixed with other clauses, such as a post_filter, can return fewer than k results.

INCORRECT: Split the chunk index into more shards on the current nodes, so that each shard contains fewer vectors.
More shards spread the same 400 million vectors over more parts of the index. A k-NN query runs on every shard and returns k results from each shard, so it still searches all the chunk vectors. The total work for each query stays about the same.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
questions.promptHtml:
A university wants an assistant for its staff. The staff policies are in Microsoft SharePoint, and the IT guides are in Confluence. Both change every week.
The assistant must answer from both systems, and each answer must reflect a change within one day. The university has no team to create or run a vector store. It wants no custom code that reads or copies the pages.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
questions.promptText:
A university wants an assistant for its staff. The staff policies are in Microsoft SharePoint, and the IT guides are in Confluence. Both change every week.
The assistant must answer from both systems, and each answer must reflect a change within one day. The university has no team to create or run a vector store. It wants no custom code that reads or copies the pages.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with a SharePoint data source and a Confluence data source, and set a daily sync schedule on each data source.
Create an AWS Lambda function that copies the SharePoint and Confluence pages to an Amazon S3 bucket each night. Create a Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with an S3 data source on that bucket.
Create an Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection and a vector index. Create a knowledge base on this vector store with a SharePoint data source and a Confluence data source, and sync both each day.
Create an Amazon Bedrock agent with action groups that call AWS Lambda functions, which the team writes to search SharePoint and Confluence for each question.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Create a Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with a SharePoint data source and a Confluence data source, and set a daily sync schedule on each data source.
With a Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base, Amazon Bedrock manages the ingestion, the storage, the indexing and the retrieval, so no team creates or runs a vector store. This type of knowledge base has native connectors, and SharePoint and Confluence are among them, so the university writes no code to read the pages. A daily sync schedule on each data source makes Amazon Bedrock sync the pages every day. So an answer reflects a change within one day.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.4.4: "Use AWS services to create integration components to connect with resources"
Example: "document management systems"

Sources:

  • Build a managed knowledge base
  • Connect a data source
  • Connect a data source to your knowledge base

INCORRECT: Create an AWS Lambda function that copies the SharePoint and Confluence pages to an Amazon S3 bucket each night. Create a Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with an S3 data source on that bucket.
This design can work, because a Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base can use an S3 data source. However, the Lambda function is custom code that reads and copies the pages, and the university wants no such code. The team must also keep this function working when SharePoint or Confluence changes. The native connectors read both systems with no code of its own.

INCORRECT: Create an Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection and a vector index. Create a knowledge base on this vector store with a SharePoint data source and a Confluence data source, and sync both each day.
A knowledge base on a vector store that the university creates is a Customer-managed Knowledge Base. In this type, the customer chooses, provisions, scales and updates the vector store. The university has no team to create or run a vector store, so this solution breaks a stated requirement. Also, since September 30, 2026, new SharePoint and Confluence connectors can no longer be created on a Customer-managed Knowledge Base.

INCORRECT: Create an Amazon Bedrock agent with action groups that call AWS Lambda functions, which the team writes to search SharePoint and Confluence for each question.
An agent can call action groups while it answers a question. Here, the team must write and maintain Lambda functions that read SharePoint and Confluence, which is the custom code that the university wants to avoid. Each answer would also depend on how well this custom search finds the right page.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
questions.promptHtml:
An insurance company runs a claims assistant that calls the RetrieveAndGenerate API of an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. The knowledge base uses an Amazon Titan Text Embeddings model and an Amazon OpenSearch Serverless vector store. Its Amazon S3 data source contains claim guides in English and German.
In tests, a Cohere Embed Multilingual model found better chunks for German questions. The team will move the assistant to this model. The assistant must keep answering during the move. The new setup must pass the team's tests before users see it.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements?
Select TWO.
questions.promptText:
An insurance company runs a claims assistant that calls the RetrieveAndGenerate API of an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. The knowledge base uses an Amazon Titan Text Embeddings model and an Amazon OpenSearch Serverless vector store. Its Amazon S3 data source contains claim guides in English and German.
In tests, a Cohere Embed Multilingual model found better chunks for German questions. The team will move the assistant to this model. The assistant must keep answering during the move. The new setup must pass the team's tests before users see it.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements?
Select TWO.

options.text: Create a new knowledge base with the Cohere Embed Multilingual model and a data source on the same S3 bucket, and sync the data source.
Update the existing knowledge base to use the Cohere Embed Multilingual model, and start a new sync to create new embeddings for every guide.
Add a second data source on the same bucket to the existing knowledge base, set this data source to the Cohere Embed Multilingual model, and sync it.
Delete the existing knowledge base first, and then create a new knowledge base with the Cohere Embed Multilingual model and sync it.
Run the test questions of the team against the new knowledge base, and then change the knowledge base ID in the configuration of the assistant.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Create a new knowledge base with the Cohere Embed Multilingual model and a data source on the same S3 bucket, and sync the data source.
The embedding model is part of the configuration of a knowledge base, and the UpdateKnowledgeBase API does not allow a change to it. So the way to use the new model is a new knowledge base with the Cohere Embed Multilingual model. Its sync reads the guides from the same bucket and creates new vectors with the new model. The old knowledge base keeps serving the assistant while this happens.

CORRECT: Run the test questions of the team against the new knowledge base, and then change the knowledge base ID in the configuration of the assistant.
The new setup must pass the tests before users see it. The test questions check the new knowledge base while users still use the old one. When the tests pass, the team changes only the knowledge base ID that the assistant sends in each RetrieveAndGenerate request. The assistant keeps answering during the whole move.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.4.5: "Design and deploy data maintenance systems to ensure that vector stores contain current and accurate information for FM augmentation"

Sources:

  • UpdateKnowledgeBase
  • VectorIngestionConfiguration
  • Supported models and Regions for Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases

INCORRECT: Update the existing knowledge base to use the Cohere Embed Multilingual model, and start a new sync to create new embeddings for every guide.
The UpdateKnowledgeBase API page says that the knowledgeBaseConfiguration field, which specifies the embedding model, cannot change. An update must send the same configuration as when the team created the knowledge base. So the existing knowledge base cannot move to the Cohere model, and a new sync would create vectors with the Titan model again.

INCORRECT: Add a second data source on the same bucket to the existing knowledge base, set this data source to the Cohere Embed Multilingual model, and sync it.
A data source has settings for how to ingest its documents, such as chunking and parsing. It has no setting for the embedding model, which belongs to the knowledge base itself. A second data source in the existing knowledge base would still use the Titan model.

INCORRECT: Delete the existing knowledge base first, and then create a new knowledge base with the Cohere Embed Multilingual model and sync it.
This order removes the knowledge base that the assistant uses before the new one is ready. From the time of the delete until the new sync ends, the assistant cannot answer, and the team has no chance to test the new setup before users see it.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
questions.promptHtml:
A chemical manufacturer is building an assistant for its lab staff. The safety data sheets and lab reports in Amazon S3 use internal product codes, such as PX-4410, and lab terms that are rare in public text.
The team must choose an Amazon Titan Text Embeddings model or a Cohere Embed English model for an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. Staff wrote 300 real questions with correct answers. The team has not chosen the text model for answers yet. The result must show the effect of the embedding model only.
Which combination of steps should the team take?
Select TWO.
questions.promptText:
A chemical manufacturer is building an assistant for its lab staff. The safety data sheets and lab reports in Amazon S3 use internal product codes, such as PX-4410, and lab terms that are rare in public text.
The team must choose an Amazon Titan Text Embeddings model or a Cohere Embed English model for an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. Staff wrote 300 real questions with correct answers. The team has not chosen the text model for answers yet. The result must show the effect of the embedding model only.
Which combination of steps should the team take?
Select TWO.

options.text: Compare the scores of the two models on a public retrieval benchmark, and choose the model with the higher score.
Create two test knowledge bases on the same documents with the same chunking settings, one with each embedding model, and sync both.
Run a retrieve-and-generate RAG evaluation job in Amazon Bedrock on each test knowledge base with the staff questions, and compare the correctness scores.
Run a retrieve-only RAG evaluation job in Amazon Bedrock on each test knowledge base with questions that a model writes from public chemistry articles.
Run a retrieve-only RAG evaluation job in Amazon Bedrock on each test knowledge base with the staff questions and answers, and compare the context relevance and context coverage scores.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Create two test knowledge bases on the same documents with the same chunking settings, one with each embedding model, and sync both.
A fair comparison of two embedding models keeps everything else the same. Two test knowledge bases on the same documents and with the same chunking settings differ only in the embedding model. Each sync creates vectors for the safety data sheets and lab reports with one of the two models.

CORRECT: Run a retrieve-only RAG evaluation job in Amazon Bedrock on each test knowledge base with the staff questions and answers, and compare the context relevance and context coverage scores.
A retrieve-only RAG evaluation job scores the chunks that each knowledge base returns, and it generates no answers. So no model that writes answers is part of the result. The staff questions contain the real product codes and lab terms of the company. Context relevance shows if the returned chunks fit each question. Context coverage needs the correct answers as ground truth, and it shows how much of each answer the returned chunks include.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.5.2: "Select and configure optimal embedding solutions to create efficient vector representations for semantic search"
Example: "by evaluating performance characteristics of Amazon Bedrock embedding models"

Sources:

  • Creating a retrieve-only RAG evaluation job
  • Create a prompt dataset for retrieve-only RAG evaluation jobs
  • Creating a retrieve-and-generate RAG evaluation job

INCORRECT: Compare the scores of the two models on a public retrieval benchmark, and choose the model with the higher score.
A public benchmark measures each model on public text. It does not show how a model handles codes such as PX-4410 or the rare lab terms in these documents. The team already has 300 real questions, which test the models on the documents that matter.

INCORRECT: Run a retrieve-and-generate RAG evaluation job in Amazon Bedrock on each test knowledge base with the staff questions, and compare the correctness scores.
A retrieve-and-generate job also uses a text model to write each answer, and the correctness score rates that answer. The score then depends on the text model as well as on the embedding model. The team has not chosen the text model, and the result must show the effect of the embedding model only.

INCORRECT: Run a retrieve-only RAG evaluation job in Amazon Bedrock on each test knowledge base with questions that a model writes from public chemistry articles.
The job type is right, but the questions do not fit this choice. Questions from public chemistry articles do not use the internal product codes and lab terms of the company. They do not test how each model finds passages in these documents, and the 300 staff questions do.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
questions.promptHtml:
A TV broadcaster runs an assistant for its production staff. The assistant uses an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base with an Amazon OpenSearch Serverless vector store. The data source is an Amazon S3 bucket with about 800 show plans and talent contracts.
Staff ask questions such as "Which presenters on shows filmed in Lisbon have contracts that end this year?" A show plan names its presenters and its filming city. A contract names one presenter and an end date, but no show and no city. The answers often miss presenters. The team wants no new metadata that someone must keep up to date.
Which change will give complete answers to these questions?
questions.promptText:
A TV broadcaster runs an assistant for its production staff. The assistant uses an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base with an Amazon OpenSearch Serverless vector store. The data source is an Amazon S3 bucket with about 800 show plans and talent contracts.
Staff ask questions such as "Which presenters on shows filmed in Lisbon have contracts that end this year?" A show plan names its presenters and its filming city. A contract names one presenter and an end date, but no show and no city. The answers often miss presenters. The team wants no new metadata that someone must keep up to date.
Which change will give complete answers to these questions?

options.text: Turn on hybrid search in the queries to the knowledge base, so each search combines vector matches with matches on the raw text.
Add a filming_city metadata attribute to each document, and filter each search on the city that the question names.
Change the chunking strategy of the data source to hierarchical chunking, so each search returns the larger parent chunks.
Create a knowledge base on the same S3 bucket that uses Amazon Neptune Analytics graphs (GraphRAG) as its vector store.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Create a knowledge base on the same S3 bucket that uses Amazon Neptune Analytics graphs (GraphRAG) as its vector store.
GraphRAG in Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases finds the entities in the documents and the relationships between them, such as a presenter who appears in a show plan and in a contract. After the first vector search, it follows these relationships to related chunks. This helps when an answer needs facts from several documents, as in this question. GraphRAG supports only Amazon S3 as the data source, and a data source can have up to 1000 files, so the bucket of about 800 documents fits.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.5.3: "Deploy and configure vector search solutions to enable semantic search capabilities for FM augmentation"

Sources:

  • Build a knowledge base with Amazon Neptune Analytics graphs
  • Configure and customize queries and response generation
  • How content chunking works for knowledge bases

INCORRECT: Turn on hybrid search in the queries to the knowledge base, so each search combines vector matches with matches on the raw text.
Hybrid search adds matches on the raw text to the vector matches, which helps when a question uses the same words as the documents. The problem here is different. No single document links a filming city to a contract end date. Hybrid search still returns separate chunks, with no link between a presenter in a show plan and the same presenter in a contract.

INCORRECT: Add a filming_city metadata attribute to each document, and filter each search on the city that the question names.
A metadata filter keeps only the documents whose attribute matches. A contract names no city, so it has no filming city to match, and the filter would remove every contract. The answer needs the contracts for the end dates.

INCORRECT: Change the chunking strategy of the data source to hierarchical chunking, so each search returns the larger parent chunks.
Hierarchical chunking first finds small child chunks and then returns their larger parent chunks. A parent chunk comes from the same document as its child. It gives more text from one show plan or one contract, but it does not link a show plan to a contract.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
questions.promptHtml:
A bank runs an assistant for its branch staff. An AWS Lambda function calls the Retrieve API of an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base and asks for five results. The function sends these chunks and the question to a model. Staff ask short questions about one product each.
Tests show that the search finds the chunk with the answer in the first 50 results for most questions, but often below the fifth result. To control cost, the model must receive no more than five chunks for each question.
Which combination of changes will meet these requirements?
Select TWO.
questions.promptText:
A bank runs an assistant for its branch staff. An AWS Lambda function calls the Retrieve API of an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base and asks for five results. The function sends these chunks and the question to a model. Staff ask short questions about one product each.
Tests show that the search finds the chunk with the answer in the first 50 results for most questions, but often below the fifth result. To control cost, the model must receive no more than five chunks for each question.
Which combination of changes will meet these requirements?
Select TWO.

options.text: Raise the numberOfResults value in the Retrieve request from 5 to 50, so the first search returns more chunks.
Keep five results in the Retrieve request, and add an Amazon Bedrock reranker model that puts those five chunks in a better order.
Add a reranking configuration with an Amazon Bedrock reranker model to the Retrieve request, and set it to return the five chunks with the highest scores.
Send all chunks from a larger search to the model, and add an instruction to the prompt to use only the most relevant chunks.
Raise the number of results to 50, and keep the five chunks with the highest vector scores in the Lambda function.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Raise the numberOfResults value in the Retrieve request from 5 to 50, so the first search returns more chunks.
A reranker can only reorder the chunks that the first search returns. The chunk with the answer is often below the fifth result, so a search for five results leaves it out. With 50 results, the first search includes this chunk for most questions. The numberOfResults field accepts values from 1 to 100.

CORRECT: Add a reranking configuration with an Amazon Bedrock reranker model to the Retrieve request, and set it to return the five chunks with the highest scores.
A reranker model calculates how relevant each chunk is to the question, and it reorders the results by these scores. The numberOfRerankedResults field decides how many results return after reranking. With a value of 5, the function receives the five most relevant chunks of the 50, and the model still reads no more than five chunks.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.5.4: "Create advanced search architectures to improve the relevance and accuracy of retrieved information for FM context"
Example: "Amazon Bedrock reranker models"

Sources:

  • Improve the relevance of query responses with a reranker model in Amazon Bedrock
  • KnowledgeBaseVectorSearchConfiguration
  • VectorSearchBedrockRerankingConfiguration

INCORRECT: Keep five results in the Retrieve request, and add an Amazon Bedrock reranker model that puts those five chunks in a better order.
A reranker reorders only the chunks it receives. With five results, the chunk with the answer is often not among them, so a new order cannot bring it in. The model still misses the answer.

INCORRECT: Send all chunks from a larger search to the model, and add an instruction to the prompt to use only the most relevant chunks.
This step sends many more than five chunks to the model, which breaks the limit of five chunks for each question. An instruction to use only the most relevant chunks does not reduce the input that the model reads, so the cost stays high.

INCORRECT: Raise the number of results to 50, and keep the five chunks with the highest vector scores in the Lambda function.
The vector scores give the same order as the first search. In most cases, the five chunks with the highest vector scores among 50 results are the same five chunks that a search for five results returns. The chunk with the answer stays below the fifth place, so the model still misses it.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance
questions.promptHtml:
A kitchen appliance company runs a support assistant that calls the RetrieveAndGenerate API of an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. The knowledge base contains service bulletins. Each bulletin names a product only by its model code, such as KTL-2041.
Customers name products by their sales names, such as "Aria kettle". Each question is about one product. The search often misses the right bulletin and returns bulletins for other products. The company has a list that maps each of its 60 sales names to a model code.
Which change will improve the search results?
questions.promptText:
A kitchen appliance company runs a support assistant that calls the RetrieveAndGenerate API of an Amazon Bedrock knowledge base. The knowledge base contains service bulletins. Each bulletin names a product only by its model code, such as KTL-2041.
Customers name products by their sales names, such as "Aria kettle". Each question is about one product. The search often misses the right bulletin and returns bulletins for other products. The company has a list that maps each of its 60 sales names to a model code.
Which change will improve the search results?

options.text: Add the list to a custom generation prompt template in the RetrieveAndGenerate requests, so the model uses the model codes when it writes the answer.
Add the list to a custom orchestration prompt template in the RetrieveAndGenerate requests, so the search query uses the model code of the product.
Turn on query decomposition in the RetrieveAndGenerate requests, so the knowledge base splits each question into smaller queries.
Add an Amazon Bedrock reranker model to the RetrieveAndGenerate requests, so the most relevant bulletins move to the top of the results.

questions.explanationHtml:
CORRECT: Add the list to a custom orchestration prompt template in the RetrieveAndGenerate requests, so the search query uses the model code of the product.
In Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, the orchestration prompt creates the search query from the question of the customer. With the list in a custom orchestration prompt, the model can write KTL-2041 in the search query when a customer writes Aria kettle. The search then compares the query with bulletins that use the same code. The custom template goes in the orchestrationConfiguration field of the RetrieveAndGenerate request.

Exam Guide Reference:
Skill 1.5.5: "Develop sophisticated query handling systems to improve the retrieval effectiveness and result quality for FM augmentation"

Sources:

  • Configure and customize queries and response generation
  • OrchestrationConfiguration
  • Improve the relevance of query responses with a reranker model in Amazon Bedrock

INCORRECT: Add the list to a custom generation prompt template in the RetrieveAndGenerate requests, so the model uses the model codes when it writes the answer.
The generation prompt combines the search results with the question so the model can write the answer. It runs after the search, so the search still uses the sales name and still returns bulletins for other products. The model can name the correct code in its answer, but it has no matching bulletin to answer from.

INCORRECT: Turn on query decomposition in the RetrieveAndGenerate requests, so the knowledge base splits each question into smaller queries.
Query decomposition splits a complex question into smaller queries. Here each question is about one product, so a split adds little. Each smaller query would still use the sales name, so the search would still miss bulletins that use only the model code.

INCORRECT: Add an Amazon Bedrock reranker model to the RetrieveAndGenerate requests, so the most relevant bulletins move to the top of the results.
A reranker model reorders the results that the search returns. The right bulletin is often not in these results, so a new order cannot bring it in. The reranker also has no list that links a sales name to a model code.

Each application has its own code that creates an embedding of the question and searches an Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection. Each application then sends the results to its own model with its own prompt.
The company may change its vector store more than once in the coming years. A change of vector store must need no change to the code of the four applications. The company wants to maintain no retrieval code of its own.
Which design will meet these requirements?

options.text: Store the collection endpoint and the index name in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, and have each application read both values when it starts.
Create one AWS Lambda function that creates an embedding of each question and searches the collection, and change each application to call this function.
Create a knowledge base in Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases on the travel guides, and change each application to call the Retrieve API with the knowledge base ID from its configuration.
Move the vectors to Amazon S3 Vectors now, and change each application to create an embedding of the question and query the vector index through the Amazon S3 Vectors API.

CORRECT: Create a knowledge base in Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases on the travel guides, and change each application to call the Retrieve API with the knowledge base ID from its configuration.
The Retrieve API returns the chunks of a knowledge base that are most relevant to a question. The knowledge base uses its embedding model to create the vector of the question and searches its own vector index, so the applications contain no embedding or search code. Each application still sends the chunks to its own model with its own prompt.

Example: "standardized API patterns for retrieval augmentation"

  • How Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases work
  • Prerequisites for using a vector store you created for a knowledge base

INCORRECT: Store the collection endpoint and the index name in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, and have each application read both values when it starts.
Parameter Store keeps the endpoint and the index name out of the code. However, each application still has code that creates the embedding and sends an OpenSearch query. Another vector store needs other query code, so all four applications must change at each move.

INCORRECT: Create one AWS Lambda function that creates an embedding of each question and searches the collection, and change each application to call this function.
One shared function hides the vector store from the four applications, so their code could stay the same at a move. However, the function is retrieval code that the company writes and maintains, and its code must change at each move. The company wants to maintain no retrieval code of its own.

INCORRECT: Move the vectors to Amazon S3 Vectors now, and change each application to create an embedding of the question and query the vector index through the Amazon S3 Vectors API.
This step changes the vector store once, but each application still contains its own embedding and query code, now written for Amazon S3 Vectors. The next change of vector store would need a change in all four applications again. The company would also keep maintaining retrieval code.
